harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: node1 now serves the preserved staged trees on TCP/8080. Public content is anonymous, staff content requires HTTP Basic authentication as reader, credentials and directory listings are inaccessible, and all behavior persisted across a verified node restart.
actions_performed: Installed the RHEL-supported Apache packages without changing the operating-system release or kernel.
Configured /public and /staff aliases with directory indexes disabled.
Created a restricted bcrypt password file outside the served tree using the supplied demonstration password.
Enabled persistent firewalld and SELinux authorization for TCP/8080.
Enabled Apache at boot and completed the mandatory node1 restart/recovery test.
Retained a root-only rollback copy at /etc/httpd/conf/httpd.conf.pre-web-auth-boundary.

evidence.requirement: Publish public and staff trees on TCP/8080
evidence.summary: Apache is enabled and listening on 8080; public and authenticated staff responses are byte-identical to the staged files.

evidence.requirement: Public anonymous; staff requires reader Basic authentication
evidence.summary: Public returns 200 anonymously; staff returns 401 without or with incorrect credentials and 200 with the supplied reader credentials. A Basic challenge is present.

evidence.requirement: Protect credentials and prevent directory listings
evidence.summary: access.txt remains root-owned mode 0600 and returns 404 directly and through a traversal-shaped request; the generated hash file is root:apache mode 0640 outside served paths; root returns 403 without a listing marker.
The original tree remains under /srv/legacy2/web-authentication-boundary, with identical file fingerprints before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: SELinux and firewall security controls remain enforced
evidence.summary: SELinux remains Enforcing with persistent content and port labels; firewalld remains active with TCP/8080 authorized.

Captured healthy baseline boot ID 03273aa8-4706-4e1c-a855-c6ae9635951d, acknowledged a native systemd reboot, observed changed boot ID 699a1ae1-06a0-46d5-9cba-4b64146f09a9, and proved full post-restart service, security, and data recovery.
